The change from the loud spear-vs-sword chant to a swaying, teasing dance rhythm caught the crowd off guard. Archers and a few younger listeners turned the number into physical play: mimed drawing bows, side-steps, exaggerated aiming and mock shots at friends. Spear fighters heckled that the archers were dancing instead of fighting; archers answered with mock shots and laughter. Several women and non-fighters enjoyed the dance quality more than the prior weapon songs, while some older fighters simply watched or drifted away. The market continued operating.
